docs.title: Arete
docs.text: One-way sync from an Obsidian vault to Anki. You write cards in a note's frontmatter; arete pushes them to Anki. Obsidian is the source of truth: nothing is written back except the ids Arete assigns.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
uv tool install git+https://github.com/adamtrnguyen/Arete
arete init          # pick the vault, the Anki media folder and the backend

On Windows, install uv first (PowerShell: powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"), run the same uv tool install, then uv tool update-shell so that arete (%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\arete.exe) is on PATH. Restart Obsidian afterwards.

From the latest release:

File Goes to main.js, manifest.json, styles.css <vault>/.obsidian/plugins/arete/ (Obsidian plugin) arete_ankiconnect.ankiaddon Anki → Tools → Add-ons → Install from file

docs.title: 2. Write a card
docs.text:
Add this to the top of any note:

---
arete: true
deck: "Biology::Anatomy"
cards:
  - Front: What are the three layers of the skin?
    Back: |-
      Epidermis, dermis, hypodermis.
  - model: Cloze
    Text: |-
      The {{c1::epidermis}} is the outermost layer of skin.
---

Leave out id: and anki:. Arete writes both on the first sync.

  • Card schema: every key, note types, deck and tag rules.
  • Writing cards: line breaks, math, cloze, dependencies.

docs.title: 3. Sync
docs.text:
arete sync --dry-run    # show what would change
arete sync

docs.title: 4. Study in prerequisite order
docs.text:
List what a card needs first under deps.requires, then:

arete queue --deck "Biology" --dry-run
arete queue --deck "Biology"      # fills the Arete::Queue filtered deck

docs.title: More
docs.text:
• arete <command> --help for every flag; CLI reference.
  • Obsidian plugin, Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Arete CLI Guide
docs.text: Commands, options and configuration for the arete command-line tool. arete <command> --help lists every flag.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
arete uses uv for dependencies and isolated environments.

git clone https://github.com/adamtrnguyen/Arete
cd Arete
uv sync

docs.title: Root Commands
docs.text: Command Description arete sync Standard sync from Obsidian to Anki. arete sync --prune Sync, then list the Arete notes whose card left the vault and ask before deleting them. arete sync --prune --yes The same, without asking. arete sync --force Re-send every card, ignoring the content cache. It does not confirm a prune. arete queue Build Arete::Queue from due cards and resolved prerequisites. arete init Initialize a new vault configuration. arete logs Open the run logs directory. arete report Show or clear card issues reported from Anki review sessions (--json, --clear N). Clearing a report unsuspends its card.

docs.title: Vault Maintenance (arete vault)
docs.text: Command Description arete vault check PATH Validate a single file for arete compatibility (--json). Reports an Arete id declared by two cards of the file (case-insensitive). It cannot see ids shared between files: arete graph check reports them, and a sync refuses them. arete vault fix PATH Auto-fix common format errors in a file. arete vault format [PATH] Normalize YAML frontmatter serialization.

docs.title: Anki Management (arete anki)
docs.text: Command Description arete anki stats Fetch card statistics for given Note IDs. arete anki browse Open Anki browser with a query. arete anki decks Print every deck name as JSON: {"decks": [...]}. arete anki queue-deck --ids JSON Fill a filtered deck with the cards of the given Arete ids, in order. Prints {"ok", "message"}. --deck-name picks the deck (default Arete Study Queue); --no-reschedule stops reviews in it from counting. arete anki suspend Suspend cards by CID. arete anki unsuspend Unsuspend cards by CID. arete anki model-css MODEL Get CSS styling for a model. arete anki model-templates MODEL Get templates for a model.

docs.title: Other
docs.text: Command Description arete config show View current resolved configuration. arete config open Open the config file in your editor. arete graph check Check dependency graph health: cycles, isolated cards, unresolved references, duplicate Arete ids (case-insensitive, as the sync compares them), unparsed files. arete graph export Print the resolved dependency graph as JSON.

docs.title: Advanced Sync Options
docs.text:
• --dry-run: Preview changes without applying to Anki.
  • --clear-cache: Empty the content cache first, so every file is parsed again.
  • --prune: Delete Anki notes Arete created whose card is gone from the vault, and decks that hold only such notes. A note without an Arete id tag (arete_ + 26-char ULID) is never deleted, whatever deck it is in, and neither is a note whose Arete id a vault card still declares. Empty decks are listed, not deleted. Prune runs only on a whole-vault sync. It shows what it will delete and asks; off a terminal it deletes nothing and reports the list. A run with any error deletes nothing, even with --yes: it lists what it would delete and says why. The summary line states the prune's outcome.
  • --yes, -y: Confirm the prune without the prompt.
  • --force: Re-send every card, ignoring the content cache. It does not confirm a prune.
  • --backend: Select backend (auto, ankiconnect, direct).
  • --workers: Override parallel sync worker count.
  • --json: Print one JSON object on stdout and nothing else; logs go to stderr. It never asks: without --yes a prune returns its preview and deletes nothing. Exit codes are those of the plain command. A sync refused by the lock (exit 75) or stopped by SIGTERM (exit 143) still prints the object, with ok false and the line it wrote to stderr as message.
Key Type Meaning ok bool The run completed without a failure (exit code 0). generated int Cards compared with Anki. changed int Cards added or updated in Anki. errors int Errors recorded during the run. message str or null Why the run failed or stopped early, such as an outdated add-on. prune object or null Null without --prune. Otherwise {status, message, notes: [{nid, arete_id, deck}], decks, note_count, deck_count, empty_decks_not_deleted, decks_kept}. status is deleted when the listed notes and decks were deleted, unconfirmed for a preview, and failed when Anki refused a delete (its message says which). Any other value means nothing was deleted.

One sync runs at a time per cache database. A sync started while another holds the lock (cache.db.lock beside the cache) does nothing: it prints one line on stderr, starting Another Arete sync is running, so this sync did nothing., and exits with status 75. A dry run takes the lock too. Exit status 1 is a sync that ran and failed.

Every write of a note (ids, vault format, vault fix) replaces the file whole, so a sync killed while writing leaves the note as it was or as written, never cut short. Sent SIGTERM, a sync stops at its next step, between file writes, and exits with status 143.

docs.title: Queue (Dependency-Sorted Study Sessions)
docs.text:
Arete supports dependency-aware study queues. By tagging notes with prerequisites, you can generate filtered decks in Anki that ensure you learn concepts in dependency order.

  • Queue output deck name is fixed: Arete::Queue.
  • With --deck, the queue is isolated to that deck unless --cross-deck is passed.
  • --depth sets how many prerequisite levels to walk (default 2). --include-new adds unreviewed cards.
  • --algo picks the ordering: static (default) collects due cards plus their prerequisites in prerequisite order, dynamic orders by a ready frontier.
# Build queue for a specific deck (due cards only)
uv run arete queue --deck "Research Methodology"

# Include new/unreviewed cards
uv run arete queue --deck "Research Methodology" --include-new

# Pull in prerequisites from other decks
uv run arete queue --deck "Research Methodology" --include-new --cross-deck

# Preview without creating deck
uv run arete queue --dry-run

# Print the preview as JSON: deck, due_count, total_with_prereqs, queue
# (each queue item: position, id, title, file as a vault-relative path with "/", is_prereq)
uv run arete queue PATH --dry-run --json

# All due cards across all decks
uv run arete queue

# Use dynamic ready-frontier ordering
uv run arete queue --algo dynamic

docs.title: Configuration (~/.config/arete/config.toml)
docs.text:
vault_root = "/path/to/vault"
anki_media_dir = "/path/to/anki/collection.media"
backend = "auto"  # 'auto' (default), 'ankiconnect', or 'direct'
prune = false

The vault root names the vault in every card's source field and link, and is where images are looked up. When vault_root (or ARETE_VAULT_ROOT) is unset, or does not hold the path given, the vault is the nearest folder at or above the path that holds .obsidian. A folder in no such vault is its own vault. A file in none is refused: set vault_root, or sync the vault folder.

[!IMPORTANT] WSL media sync: arete copies images into the Anki media directory, so the path must be reachable from WSL, for example /mnt/c/Users/.../collection.media.

docs.title: Arete Plugin Guide
docs.text: The Arete Obsidian plugin adds sync, card health, graph and study queue views on top of the arete CLI.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the latest main.js, manifest.json, and styles.css from GitHub Releases.
  2. Create a folder: <Vault>/.obsidian/plugins/arete.
  3. Place the 3 files into that folder and enable the plugin in Obsidian settings.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
• Sync on save: off by default. When on, a Markdown file syncs after Obsidian writes it to disk (autosave included) and the setting Debounce delay (ms) passes without another write.
  • Manual sync: click the ribbon icon Sync to Anki (Arete), click the status bar item, or run the Sync command. The plugin sets no default hotkey; bind one in Settings, Hotkeys.
  • Other commands: Sync current file, Sync (prune deleted cards), Sync (force re-upload all).

docs.title: Card health and gutter
docs.text:
The card gutter marks each card in the open note: - Index number: the card's position in the current file. - Health bar: the card's worst state among lapses, difficulty, retrievability, stability and (SM-2 only) ease. Green is fine, orange a warning, red an error. Grey is a card not yet synced. - Difficulty or ease: FSRS difficulty out of 10, or SM-2 ease (E:nn%). - Lapse counter: the lapse count (3L), orange from 1 and red at the lapse threshold.

The thresholds are in the settings under Card health analysis.

docs.title: Queue builder
docs.text: Build a filtered deck that puts prerequisites first: 1. Run Open dashboard (or click the dashboard ribbon icon) and pick the Queue builder tab. 2. Choose a deck filter (default All decks), a prerequisite depth and a max card count. 3. Click Build queue to see the cards in prerequisite order. 4. Click Send to Anki to create the filtered deck Arete Study Queue.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• Graphs: Open local graph and Open global graph draw deps.requires edges; hovering a node previews its card.
  • Editing: edit deps in the note, or in the card editor (Open YAML editor).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
• Python executable: arete, the command uv tool install puts on PATH, or a full path to it (on Windows %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\arete.exe). A Python with Arete installed also works: python3 on macOS and Linux, python or py on Windows (a bare python3 runs python there). Quote a path that holds a space. A .cmd or .bat file is refused; point at the .exe.
  • Project root: the Arete checkout (the folder with pyproject.toml). Needed only when the plugin runs Arete through uv run.
  • Parallel workers: sync workers, 1 to 16.
  • Test configuration: the Test button runs the Python executable setting with --help and says whether Arete started.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Logs: check the developer console (Cmd+Option+I) or the run_*.log files that arete logs opens.
  • Environment: the Test button in settings verifies the Python environment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: Common problems and how to fix them.

docs.title: 1. Connection Issues (AnkiConnect)
docs.text:
If Arete cannot reach Anki:

  • Anki closed?: Arete writes the collection directly (the default auto backend).
  • Anki open?: Arete needs the arete_ankiconnect add-on (ANKI_PLUGIN.md). It replaces AnkiConnect: do not install both.
  • Port Binding: The add-on listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 (webBindAddress, webBindPort).
  • Allowed Origins: In Anki, Tools -> Add-ons -> arete_ankiconnect -> Config: make sure your origin is in webCorsOriginList (http://localhost by default).

docs.title: 2. WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)
docs.text:
WSL users often face networking hurdles because WSL 2 uses a virtualized network.

  • The curl.exe Bridge: arete attempts to use curl.exe (the Windows host binary) to communicate with Anki running on Windows. Ensure curl.exe is in your Windows PATH and accessible from WSL.
  • Firewall: Ensure Windows Firewall isn't blocking incoming connections to port 8765.

docs.title: 3. Python Environment (uv)
docs.text:
• Command not found: arete: uv tool install puts arete in ~/.local/bin (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin). Run uv tool update-shell, then open a new terminal and restart Obsidian. In a checkout, run uv run arete.
  • Windows: "another program has open": Windows cannot replace a note another program holds open (an editor, a sync client, a virus scanner). Arete waits about 1.5 s, then fails that file's cards with this message and leaves the note as it was. Close the program and sync again.
  • Dependency Errors: Run uv sync to ensure all dependencies are correctly installed.

docs.title: 4. Sync Gaps & Missing Cards
docs.text:
• "File skipped": If a file isn't syncing, check that its frontmatter has arete: true and a non-empty cards: list. arete vault check <file> says what is missing.
  • Card refused as a duplicate: the same Arete id on two cards, or the same first field in one deck and note type, is refused and named in the output. arete graph check lists shared ids.
  • Stale cache: arete sync --clear-cache empties the content cache and parses every file again.

docs.title: 5. Locating Logs
docs.text:
When all else fails, check the logs. They contain detailed stack traces and internal logic transitions.

uv run arete logs

This will open the directory containing your run_*.log files. Attach the latest log to any GitHub issue you open.

docs.title: Arete card schema
docs.text: What Arete reads from a note's frontmatter. Style (how to write it so it renders) is in FORMAT.md.

docs.title: File-Level Frontmatter
docs.text:
A file is an Arete note when its frontmatter has arete: true and a non-empty cards list.

---
arete: true                        # Required marker
deck: "Parent::Child"              # Anki deck, :: for nesting. Required at file or card level.
model: "Basic"                     # Default note type. Options: Basic, Cloze, or custom model name.
tags: [tag1, tag2]                 # Applied to all cards in file
cards:
  - ...                            # Required, non-empty list
---

docs.title: Card Schema — Basic Model
docs.text:
cards:
  - id: arete_01KFA531FYFDAHH1RXBXGE3ZNX   # Auto-generated ULID on first sync if missing
    Front: "Question text"                   # Required, non-empty
    Back: |-                                 # Required, non-empty. Use |- for multiline.
      Answer text
      with multiple lines
    deck: "Override::Deck"                   # Optional, overrides file-level deck
    model: "Basic"                           # Optional, overrides file-level model
    tags: [extra-tag]                        # Optional, added to the file-level tags
    deps:
      requires: [arete_ULID, basename]       # Prerequisites (card IDs or filenames without .md)
      related: [arete_ULID]                  # Related cards (informational, not traversed)
    anki:                                    # Written by Arete after sync — do not manually set
      nid: "1767401291489"
      cid: "1767583698928"

docs.title: Card Schema — Cloze Model
docs.text:
cards:
  - id: arete_01KFA531FYFDAHH1RXBXGE3ZN9
    model: Cloze
    Text: "The {{c1::epidermis}} is the {{c2::outermost}} layer of skin."   # Required
    "Back Extra": "Additional context"                                       # Optional

docs.title: Card Schema — Custom Models
docs.text: Any field name not in the reserved set becomes an Anki field. At least one field required. Reserved keys: model, deck, tags, id, deps, anki

docs.title: Key Rules
docs.text:
• IDs: arete_ prefix + 26-char ULID. Auto-generated on first sync. Do not fabricate. The same id on two cards is refused: neither syncs.
  • Sync overwrites Anki. Every sync sets the fields, deck, tags and note type of a card's Anki note to the vault's, except the tags leech and marked, which stay.
  • Finding the note: by anki.nid, then by the Arete id tag, then by the first field. A card whose first field already exists in the same deck and note type is refused.
  • Tags are stored as Anki stores them: a tag with a space becomes two tags.
  • anki.nid / anki.cid: Written by Arete after sync. Never manually create or modify these.
  • Deck: Must be specified at file level or card level. Use :: for nesting.
  • Changing model on a synced card converts its Anki note in place: same cards, review history kept. Fields carry over by name, then Front↔Text and Back↔Back Extra. Anki counts this as a schema change, so its next AnkiWeb sync may ask for a one-way full upload.
  • Multiline content: Use YAML block scalar |- (literal, strip trailing newline).
  • Math: $...$ and $$...$$ are auto-converted to \(...\) and \[...\].
  • Images: ![[image.png]] wikilinks and ![](image.png) are auto-resolved and copied to Anki media.
  • No duplicate YAML keys: Arete uses a strict YAML loader that rejects duplicates.
  • No tabs in YAML: Use spaces only.
  • Deps references: an arete_ULID (one card), a basename like algebra (all cards in algebra.md), or folder/Name when several files share a basename.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
---
arete: true
deck: "Biology::Human Anatomy"
model: Basic
tags: [anatomy, high-retention]
cards:
  - id: arete_01KFA531FYFDAHH1RXBXGE3ZNX
    Front: What are the three layers of the skin?
    Back: |-
      1. Epidermis (outer)
      2. Dermis (middle, contains collagen)
      3. Hypodermis (inner, fat layer)
    deps:
      requires: []
      related: [arete_01KFA531FYFDAHH1RXBXGE3ZN9]

  - id: arete_01KFA531FYFDAHH1RXBXGE3ZN9
    model: Cloze
    Text: The {{c1::epidermis}} is the {{c2::outermost}} layer of skin.
    "Back Extra": Contains melanocytes for pigmentation
---

docs.title: Arete card YAML — format guide
docs.text: How to write cards: so a card renders the same in Obsidian and in Anki. Schema lives in SCHEMA.md; this file is the style. Rules marked 📏 were measured against arete's converter.

docs.title: The shape
docs.text:
cards:
  - Front: |-
      What does FlashAttention tile into SRAM?
    Back: |-
      Blocks of $Q$, $K$ and $V$, sized so each fits in on-chip SRAM.

      This keeps the $N \times N$ score matrix out of HBM.
    Back Extra: |-
      (Dao et al., *FlashAttention*, §3.1)
    deps:
      requires: [Self-Attention]
      related: []
Rule Why Question field first (Front, or Text for Cloze), then answer fields, then deps Scans top-down like the card. id and anki last, and only Arete writes them Arete appends them on first sync. Back Extra holds citations and asides, not the answer It is the extra field of the Cloze note type. Multi-line value → \|- block Keeps backslashes and quotes literal.

docs.title: Line breaks 📏
docs.text:
arete's converter runs Python-Markdown with fenced_code and tables only — no nl2br.

You write Anki shows two lines separated by one newline one line (joined with a space) a blank line between them two paragraphs - item right after a text line plain text, not a list a blank line, then - item lines a list a table right after a text line plain text, not a table a ``` fence right after a text line a code block (fences do not need the blank line)

⚠ The Obsidian Card Editor preview treats one newline as a break, so it can look right while Anki joins the lines. Use blank lines. Never end lines with two spaces for a hard break: a rewrite by arete's YAML writer turns such a value into one double-quoted line.

docs.title: Backslashes and escaping
docs.text:
In a |- block every character is literal. Write LaTeX exactly as in a note.

Right (\|- block) Wrong Renders as $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$ $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$ a line break (\) then the letters "alpha" a real line break typed as two characters the literal text "quoted" inside code "quoted" backslashes in the card

In a double-quoted scalar ("...") YAML does interpret \ and , another reason to prefer |-.

docs.title: Math
docs.text: Rule Detail Inline $...$, display $$...$$ Converted to \(...\) and \[...\] for Anki. Display math: $$ on its own lines Keep the formula lines between them. $\sim$100x is math Obsidian and Arete both read it as math, so $ needs a closing pair. State shapes on first use e.g. x ∈ ℝᵈ, not a bare x ∈ ℝ for a vector.

docs.title: Cloze
docs.text:
- model: Cloze
    Text: |-
      FlashAttention uses the {{c1::online softmax}} trick with a running {{c2::max and sum::two statistics}}.
    Back Extra: |-
      (Dao et al., §3.1)
  • {{cN::answer}} or {{cN::answer::hint}}. Same N = hidden together on one card.
  • A deletion ends at the first }}. 📏 {{c1::$e^{x^{2}}$}} is cut to $e^{x^{2; write {{c1::$e^{x^{2} }$}} (space between the braces). Anki's cloze renderer cuts at the first }} too (checked against the bundled anki library).
  • The Card Editor preview shows the lowest cN.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Form Resolves to arete_<ULID> that one card Note Name every card in the one file with that name folder/Note Name picks one when several files share the name a single value (requires: Algebra) allowed; a list is clearer

requires = must know first (walked by the queue). related = peers (not walked). A ref to a note with no cards, or to a missing note, is reported by arete graph check.

docs.title: Never in card fields
docs.text:
• Footnote markers [^id] — Anki has no footnotes; cite inline, e.g. (Author, p. 12).
  • id: / anki: you made up — Arete issues both.
  • Tabs — YAML forbids them; use spaces.
  • Duplicate keys — Arete's loader rejects the file.

docs.title: Check before handing back
docs.text:
1. arete vault check "<note>.md" passes.
  2. No \\ before a letter, no literal \n, no line ending in spaces.
  3. A blank line before every list and table, and between separate paragraphs.
  4. Show the card in the Card Editor preview (SKILL.md, Workflow 2).
